articles.title: WSL: London City Lionesses showing rapid development in pursuit of Champions League football as Arsenal flop again
articles.summary: Digital journalist Laura Hunter returns for a second season with a WSL-dedicated column, analysing all the big talking points from across the weekend's action; this week's focus is on how London City have taken advantage of Arsenal's dreadful form to propel themselves into European spots
articles.body:
London City are developing at a rapid rate

A gulf is appearing at the top of the Women's Super League. By most observers estimations that is not surprising. Manchester City remain perfect so far, their momentum too compelling to resist as title favourites. Chelsea look formidable too.

What intrigues me is how far London City Lionesses have come in such a short space of time to join them as front-runners. I don't believe they have enough to upstage Man City or Chelsea, but perhaps there is merit in Michele Kang's Champions League wish after all.

Many thought this season was too soon. I still have one foot in that camp. And yet, London City are third. Five points clear of fourth-placed Tottenham, who they humbled 6-1 a fortnight ago. My stance on their staying power based on that evidence is beginning to soften.

Only Chelsea have scored more times from open play. Alexia Putellas is now wielding more influence on games, albeit she started from the bench at the weekend. The consistency of their many final-third creators, even when Putellas does not play, makes for a persuasive argument.

Opta's big chances created metric is probably the best judge of creativity flow in a team and London City rank top. There is a stylistic maturity to their game. The way they sweep forward with numbers and intensity can open up just about any defensive block, the forward line all combining for a wonderfully-worked opener against Everton at the weekend.

Danielle van de Donk's instinctive flick to unlock the zone from which Delphine Cascarino scored showed skill and, more impressive still, connectivity. The relentlessness of their press created a second opportunity for Freya Godfrey not long after, which she buried emphatically.

A squad that boasts so many attacking talents should be scoring these types of goals. There should be tactical variety and imagination. But the way Maestre has knitted all those pieces together to create a cohesive unit with clear patterns of play deserves attention.

A true measure of their stamina arrives at the beginning of next month when they host league leaders Man City. There is no greater test. No doubt they will approach it with the confidence of a side that is showing rapid development and an identifiable desire to mix it with the best in the division.

Of course one of the giants had to fall for London City to assume a place in the top three. That giant is Arsenal. Their latest flop against newly promoted Birmingham City perfectly encapsulated the mood around north London. They are this season's big losers.

The Gunners are currently on their longest winless run in the side's history. Boos could be heard from the stands at the weekend. Renee Slegers is running out of hiding places.

Her side is no longer one that plays on instinct and impulse. All their top creators appear inhibited, unable to summon the strength to break through opposition teams who choose to block rather than play. Of course that is their prerogative. Birmingham were excellent at it on Saturday.

And so Arsenal lose more ground. Confidence takes another hit. 19-year-old Lisa Baum is the only player to score more than once in the league this term - as a new signing. Leadership looks lost.

They are already well out of the running for the title with a 12-point gap to Man City at the top. Before long, they will be out of European contention, too.

Ella Toone has long been Manchester United's poster girl. A lifelong fan, who grew up supporting the club in Tyldesley, about 11 miles north of Old Trafford.

It's only right she has a place in its history books, scoring the opener in victory over Charlton at the weekend to take her level with Leah Galton as the club's leading scorer of WSL goals.

Man Utd made it three wins on the spin in the process as Eva Olid's stamp continues to become more recognisable. Toone has played a big part in that transition.

articles.title: Luis Carrión: “El Leganés tiene que ser atrevido”
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico pepinero confía en el potencial de la plantilla y apuesta por recuperar la identidad perdida
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico pepinero confía en el potencial de la plantilla y apuesta por recuperar la identidad perdida
articles.body: Luis Carrión ya ha tomado las riendas del Leganés. El técnico ha sido presentado en el Estadio Ontime Butarque, acompañado por el presidente Eduardo Cosín y el director de fútbol Andrés Pardo. Llega con el reto de cambiar la dinámica de un equipo que acumula cuatro derrotas consecutivas y que necesita recuperar cuanto antes las buenas sensaciones. El presidente explicó los motivos del relevo en el banquillo y reconoció que el problema iba más allá de los resultados. “Lo que ha sucedido desde el inicio de temporada lo resumiría en una crisis de identidad que luego ha derivado en una crisis de resultados”, Cosín defendió el potencial de una plantilla confeccionada con una importante inversión y aseguró que Carrión encaja con la filosofía futbolística que busca el club. El nuevo entrenador, que ya había mantenido conversaciones con el Leganés en anteriores ocasiones, reconoció que era uno de los destinos que más le atraían. “Al principio de temporada era una de las plantillas que pensaba que tenían más potencial”. Sobre su propuesta futbolística, dejó claras sus intenciones: «El equipo tiene que ser atrevido y creo que podemos ser un equipo que haga daño al rival”, apostando por un conjunto que busque siempre los tres puntos. Carrión también quiso transmitir tranquilidad respecto al estado del vestuario. “No he visto un equipo decaído. He visto un equipo que ha sacado malos resultados, pero no un equipo dejado”. El técnico recordó sus experiencias en Oviedo y Cartagena, donde consiguió revertir situaciones complicadas: “Encontramos soluciones y estoy convencido de que las vamos a encontrar también aquí”. Sin embargo, evitó marcarse grandes objetivos clasificatorios. “No quiero marcarme un objetivo claro. Quiero que pensemos en el domingo y que la consecuencia sea una mejora en la clasificación”. Carrión ya ha dirigido su primer entrenamiento, destacando la buena predisposición de sus futbolistas. Comienza una nueva etapa en Butarque, con la ilusión renovada y el desafío de devolver al Leganés su mejor versión.

articles.title: Ibai Gómez cumple los "microobjetivos" de ascenso con el Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: El equipo maño es colíder después de ocho jornadas
articles.summary: El equipo maño es colíder después de ocho jornadas
articles.body: Ibai Gómez nunca ha sido de mirar a largo plazo y desde su llegada al Real Zaragoza habló de cumplir unos microobjetivos. ¿De qué se trata? Para lograr el ascenso tiene en mente sumar siete puntos cada cuatro partidos y tras las primeras ocho jornadas ha cumplido los primeros dos. Po eso, los aragoneses son colíderes pese a empatar los dos últimos choques. En las primeras cuatro jornadas, los zaragocistas lograron nueve puntos y en las cuatro siguientes han firmado ocho. En total, tres puntos por encima de los mínimos exigibles, según sus cálculos, para alcanzar el ascenso directo a final de temporada. Y eso, que los blanquillos llevan dos partidos más como visitantes y este viernes volverán a jugar fuera. "Estamos dentro de los microobjetivos que marcamos. Con estos puntos, el objetivo a final de temporada se consigue, seguro. Si hablamos de microobjetivos, los hemos conseguido", indicó el técnico en sala de prensa al término del choque contra el Murcia, el más complicado hasta el momento. El tema de los microobjetivos no es nuevo para Ibai. Ya en su etapa de futbolista en el Athletic hablaba de este término para lograr las grandes metas al final del curso. Este viernes contra el Europa, el Real Zaragoza buscará comenzar con bien el tercer tramo de cuatro partidos.

articles.title: Mario Cristobal Trolls FSU with Meme of Florida After Miami's OT Win
articles.summary: After rising to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 following Saturday's overtime win over archrival Florida State, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal had a little fun on social media.
articles.body:
After rising to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 following Saturday's overtime win over archrival Florida State, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal had a little fun on social media.

Cristobal trolled the Seminoles by sharing a meme of the state of Florida emblazoned with the Hurricanes logo:

Cristobal's Miami squad passed its toughest test of the 2026 season by earning a 43-35 double-overtime win over a motivated Florida State team that was looking to play the spoiler. The Hurricanes improved to 6-0 and claimed the No. 1 spot in the Top 25 for the first time since 2002.

During Cristobal's tenure, he has rebuilt Miami into a perennial national title contender, so he has every right to revel in the team's success, even if it comes at the expense of the Hurricanes' biggest rivals.

Miami will try to remain undefeated when it hosts Pittsburgh (5-2) in another ACC showdown on Saturday.

articles.title: Who was RI's best HS football player in Week 6? Vote now to decide.
articles.summary: Which star shined brightest on the field in Week 6? We found the nominees, now it's up to you to vote for the Providence Journal Football Player of the Week.
articles.body:
Temperatures dropped this weekend, but the play on the field did not. Games are starting to mean a lot more than they did a few weeks ago and the best players in the state are showing as much when they step on the gridiron.

Finding nominees for the Week 6 Providence Journal Player of the Week wasn't hard. As always, figuring out who are five nominees should be proved to be a challenge. We knocked the list down and will let our readers decide who should be the Week 6 Player of the Week.

There's only one way to vote - check out the bios of this week's five nominees and then make you pick in the ballot at the bottom of the page. Voting opens at 9 a.m. Monday and runs through Saturday night and you can vote as many times as you'd like between then. The winner will be announced in this space next week.

The most passionate football schools are usually from the smallest communities and one of the state's smallest showed up in a huge way for one of their own.

In the race for Week 5 Providence Journal Player of the Week, North Smithfield's Brady Bouley found himself in a battle with Pilgrim's Grady Weaver. North Smithfield is the size of some Warwick neighborhoods, but it didn't matter. Bouley finished with over 50 percent of the vote, besting the 32.5 percent earned by Weaver, making Bouley the Week 5 Providence Journal Player of the Week.

Congratulations to Bouley and the North Smithfield faithful!

The prize for Providence Journal Football Player of the Week is simple – it's a big bucket of clout.

The award is designed to be an interactive way for the state's most passionate football communities to show support for their local players. We want the athletes, teams and schools to create social media campaigns to try and earn as many votes as possible. When a player wins, the community does as well – and that shows us which ones are truly passionate about high school football.

The second step is making sure someone from the team is reporting scores and statistics to the Providence Journal. On gamedays – whether its Thursday, Friday or Saturday – coaches from both teams are responsible for sending the Journal all their scoring information from the game. This information helps us put together our football roundup each week and figure out which players should be nominated.

Final score and touchdown information should be emailed to the Providence Journal at PJSports@ProvidenceJournal.com by 11 p.m. on Thursdays and Fridays and within two hours of the end of the game on Saturdays.

Once we find our candidates, the Journal may reach out to coaches for more complete statistics. Programs that do not report scoring information will not have players considered as nominees. If you think we missed your player, talk to your head coach or athletic director and ask if they are sending results to the Providence Journal.

So who will be the Week 6 Providence Journal Player of the Week? Let's take a look at the nominees and get ready to start voting now!

Borges made a statement early, then came up big late to help the Eagles pull out a 35-14 win over South Kingstown. On the first play from scrimmage, Borges went left and made a 63-yard housecall to get Barrington off to the start it was looking for. He added a second-quarter touchdown run and, up 21-14 in the fourth, slammed the door shut on SK with a third score. Borges finished the game with 14 carries for 103 yards and the three touchdown as the Eagles kept their playoff hopes alive.

The Patriots had their hands full with Chariho on Friday, but their fabulous freshman came through to help them pull out a dramatic 20-19 win. After an injury to star back Sam Waterman, Gentilella became the focal point of the offense. He finished his night with nine catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, ran for 24 yards and came up big on the game's final play, popping in the 2-point conversion for the game-winning score.

The undefeated Avengers remained that way on Friday night and showed there's more than one way to win a football game. Lehne provided points against North Providence without playing offense, sacking the quarterback in the end zone for a safety and later adding touchdown return after a blocked punt. Lehne and the defense quieted the Cougars' all evening in a 16-6 win that keeps them atop the Division III standings.

An injury has kept Sampson off the field, but the Scarlet Knights were certainly happy to see him back on the field Saturday. The senior took the offense down the field and scored on a short run for the first score against North Smithfield and led a defensive effort that quieted the big-play Northmen down. In overtime, Sampson scored on the first play and then helped the defense get the stop that clinched the 20-14 upset win.

Getting nominated has been an almost weekly occurrence for Stafford, so let's see if the Skipper fans can actually show him some support this time around. Stafford is the best offensive player in the state and continued to prove as much on Friday, rushing for 192 yards and two touchdowns, adding a fumble recovery score, in North Kingstown's 23-10 win over St. Raphael, which keeps the Skippers locked into the No. 3 seed in Division I.

articles.title: Where Alabama sits in ESPN FPI rankings following loss vs. Tennessee
articles.summary: Alabama's chances to make the College Football Playoff have taken a significant hit following the Crimson Tide's loss at Tennessee.
articles.body:
Following an ugly road loss at Tennessee, did the Alabama Crimson Tide move in ESPN's latest Football Power Index team rankings entering Week 8?

As of Sunday, Oct. 18, Alabama is ranked as the nation's No. 6 team with a FPI rating of 24.2. The No. 6 ranking was the same as this time last week , although the Crimson Tide's FPI rating a week ago after the Georgia loss was 26.6, meaning it dropped after the Tennessee defeat.

ESPN's FPI also now projects Alabama's eventual win-loss record to be 9.2-3.0 with only a 22.4% chance to win out. In terms of the other FPI percentages, Alabama now has a 12.7% chance to win the SEC, as well as 49.4% chance to make the College Football Playoff, which dropped significantly from 82.3% last week before the Tennessee game.

Alabama's chances of winning a national championship also took a significant hit, now sitting at only 4.9%.

Alabama's next game comes at home this upcoming Saturday, Oct. 24, against the Texas A&M Aggies. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III might make it hurt more vs. Seahawks in Week 7
articles.summary: Former Seattle Seahawks RB Kenneth Walker III might make it hurt more versus his old tema in Week 7.
articles.body:
The 3-3 Seattle Seahawks have a huge game in Week 7. They'll host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Lumen Field on Sunday Night Football . It'll mark the return of former Seahawks running back (and Super Bowl LX MVP) Kenneth Walker III, who is currently dominating with the Chiefs.

Walker is currently averaging 133 rushing yards per game. He's posted a league-leading 665 rushing yards . He's averaging a league-high 6.3 yards per carry and has scored eight total touchdowns as an offensive playmaker. The former Michigan State standout has been held under 100 yards just once.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks haven't run the football effectively while navigating Walker's departure. They rank 18th in rushing, averaging a rather pedestrian 107.2 yards per game. Running backs Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson, and George Holani have combined to lose four fumbles in six weeks.

The Seahawks will hopefully get Zach Charbonnet back for the Chiefs game . Charbonnet has been recovering from a torn ACL injury suffered during the playoffs last season. He's currently expected to make his 2026 debut with the Seahawks coming off of the Thursday Night Football mini bye.

The Seahawks offense undeniably misses Walker greatly. He'll attempt to make it hurt when the Chiefs visit Lumen Field on primetime in Week 7.

articles.title: Arsenal return ruled out but USMNT striker Folarin Balogun backed for Premier League transfer by title-winning former Gunners and Monaco star
articles.summary: A return to Arsenal for Folarin Balogun has been ruled out, but Gilles Grimandi has told GOAL why the USMNT striker could thrive in the Premier League when h...
articles.body:
Arsenal sold academy graduate to Monaco in 2023

Balogun was born in the United States, to Nigerian parents, but was raised in London. He joined the fabled Hale End academy at the age of eight and rose through the ranks to take in 10 competitive appearances for the Gunners.

His path to regular first-team football was forever blocked, meaning that much-needed game time and experience needed to be picked up during a couple of loan spells. One of those, at Reims, allowed Balogun to catch the eye in France.

A permanent switch to Monaco was sanctioned in 2023 , with the 25-year-old - who switched international allegiance from England to the US and now has 31 senior caps to his name - scoring 19 goals across all competitions last season.

He has been registering on recruitment radars across Europe , with Arsenal including a 17.5 per cent sell-on clause in the deal which took Balogun to Monaco. They stand to benefit from any sale, but could they explore the option of bringing a familiar face back onto their books?

Why Balogun will not head back to Emirates Stadium

The Gunners are still crying out for a prolific No.9, but two-time Premier League title winner Grimandi is not convinced that a product of their youth system is of the standard required at Emirates Stadium . The Frenchman, who also represented Monaco in his playing days and was speaking on behalf of talkSPORT Bet Online Slots , told GOAL when asked for his assessment of Balogun: "He's a good player, he's a good player in Ligue 1.

"I don't think he can go back to Arsenal. It's quite complicated, they already have [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres. So even top players, it's complicated for them to perform in this position at Arsenal.

"I don't think Balogun can bring something more than what Arteta's got at this moment, and it's still hard for them. But he's a good player, he did well last season, he played good football, he can take the space, he has a good technique. But I'm not sure that he will bring something more than what we've got at Arsenal at this time."

Asked if Balogun could make more of an impact elsewhere in England , having come close to heading for Merseyside, Grimandi added: "Maybe. I think it will be a good choice for Everton to get this guy.

"I think he can play in the Premier League of course, but the level of Arsenal is so high at this time that I'm not sure that he will help the team to get what they want to get."

USMNT star leaves Premier League transfer door open

He is still open to the idea of returning to his roots at some stage. Asked by talkSPORT if he could end up in the Premier League, the hard-working frontman said: "Yes, potentially. Football has many twists and turns as we've seen after the World Cup. I was close to a transfer, didn't materialise, but for sure it's definitely an option."
